title: Preflight liveness & capacity prober for Private (VPC) installs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective:
Build an automated pre-install 'liveness and capacity prober' that runs as part of Private (VPC) deployment pipelines and validates the critical environment requirements for a successful Redwood Private install. The prober must detect quota shortfalls, IAM misconfigurations, DNS/VPC resolution problems, and GPU SKU availability before an operator or automated installer proceeds with provisioning.

Scope:
- Terraform/IaC-integrated checks that run during CI/CD preflight (terraform plan/apply dry-run hooks).
- Lightweight, non-invasive probes that do not modify customer infra (read-only API calls + ephemeral resource queries).
- Cloud-agnostic checks (AWS first priority, GCP / Azure probes as secondary but extensible).
- Produce machine-readable report (JSON) with actionable remediation steps and severity categorization.

Non-goals:
- Full remediation automation (we only provide guidance and opt-in remediation helpers in a follow-up ticket).
- Long-running stress tests or full capacity reservation.

Design & checks to implement:
1) Quotas & SKU availability
   - Query provider APIs for available vCPU/GPU/Network ENI quota per region/account.
   - Verify requested GPU SKUs (e.g., NVIDIA A100, H100, T4) are in the provider's SKU list and return available capacity for target region. For AWS: DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings + DescribeReservedInstancesOfferings as fallback.
   - Compare requested cluster size (from IaC variables) vs available quota and flag shortfalls with exact delta.

2) IAM & permissions sanity
   - Run IAM policy simulation (cloud provider simulatePolicy or assume-role + minimal STS call) to validate that the installer principal can create roles, attach policies, create instance profiles, KMS decrypt/encrypt if required, and manage networking resources.
   - Detect common pitfalls: missing iam:PassRole, ssm:GetParameter for secrets, kms:Decrypt for customer keys.

3) DNS and VPC networking
   - Check that VPC has DNS hostnames and DNS resolution enabled.
   - Validate private hosted zone association(s) exist and that an EC2 (or equivalent) in target VPC can resolve the control-plane and agent hostnames (run a remote dig/host lookup via an ephemeral VM or use provider's DNS test APIs).

4) Control-plane liveness and TLS checks
   - If control-plane endpoint exists (customers upgrading), perform TLS certificate validation, HTTP healthcheck endpoints (/healthz) and token-based auth handshake (where applicable).

5) Upgrade-readiness simulation
   - Verify that current cluster version and target runtime/agent versions are compatible and that required node instance types are available for in-place upgrade or replacement workflows.

6) IaC semantics & plan diff checks
   - Run terraform plan and parse expected resource counts; map plan output to quotas and permissions needed, surfacing missing permissions that terraform apply would require.

Implementation notes:
- Implementation will be a small Go binary (prober-service) that runs in CI and as a local operator tool. It will use provider SDKs directly and a thin terraform-plan parser for IaC mapping.
- All provider API calls must be read-only and idempotent. Where network resolution requires an EC2 instance, the probe will use a customer-provided 'probe-host' variable (existing test instance) or execute an opt-in ephemeral probe that can be disabled by customers.
- Results are emitted as a single JSON artifact at the end of the run with fields: summary.status, summary.failed_checks (list), remediation.hints (list), raw.provider_responses (stringified).

Acceptance criteria (must be verifiable):
- The prober is invoked by the private-install CI job and produces JSON report in <= 90s for small configs and <= 5m for large configs.
- The report contains explicit quota deltas for each failed quota check and an exact list of missing IAM permissions when simulation shows lack of privileges.
- DNS resolution test verifies both A/AAAA and SRV (where applicable) records against the VPC resolver.
- A sample run with our staging account is recorded in the job artifacts and a follow-up PR demonstrates remediation docs linked in the report.

Rollout & owner:
- Engineering (Infra/Private) owns the prober. Initial owner: Devon Chen. PM partner: Laura Patel. Security reviewer: Marcus Liu.

Next steps / tasks:
- RFC for prober behavior & opt-in ephemeral probes (owner: Devon) (2d)
- Implement AWS quota/sku checks + IAM simulate (owner: Ravi Singh) (5d)
- Implement terraform-plan mapper and JSON output schema (owner: Mei Wong) (3d)
- Integrate into private-install CI and add artifact upload (owner: CI team) (2d)
- End-to-end validation in staging account and create remediation playbook (owner: SRE) (3d)
